overall: The AG found no Open Meeting Law violation: the Commission could lawfully discuss the complainant's professional competence in open session, and Purpose 1 gave him no right to compel executive session. The notice point was not separately analyzed.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the chair, a commissioner and staff discussed his character, job performance and credentials in open session without individual notice to him.
allegations.key_passage: we find that the Commission did not violate the Open Meeting Law when it discussed Mr. Marro’s professional competence in open session on August 5.

allegations.summary: Complainant contended he had a right under Purpose 1 to compel the discussion of his conduct to occur in executive session.
Complainant alleged the discussion occurred without individual notice to him while he was out of town; the letter did not separately analyze notice.
allegations.key_passage: the Open Meeting Law permits public bodies to meet in executive session for a limited number of purposes but never requires a public body to meet in executive session.

note: Read by a language model from the letter; every key passage is checked verbatim against it and dropped if not. A holding is the Attorney General’s reading of the law in this case only.
